sources.entry: Listaway - List management app for creating and publicly sharing lists of items. Supports auth, admin tools, item notes and priorities, and opt-in public read-only links with randomized URLs (alternative to Amazon Lists). (Source Code) MIT Docker

summary.one_liner: Listaway is a self-hostable app for creating lists of items (wishlists or tracking lists) and optionally sharing them publicly via randomized read-only URLs.
summary.what_it_does: Lets authenticated users, individually or as a team, create and manage lists of items, each with a name, optional URL, optional priority, and optional notes. Lists and collections (groups of lists, including shared lists) can have optional descriptions. Lists are sortable by name and priority. Lists and collections can be opted in to public read-only access via a URL containing a random string, and lists can be shared with other group members as read-only or editable. The app includes group and instance administration, email/password login with password reset, and optional OIDC/OAuth2 single sign-on. It runs against PostgreSQL and is deployed via Docker Compose using a published image.
use_cases: share a gift wishlist with family
track a list of books to read
publish a custom PC build parts list
share a list of tasks needing help
manage team lists with shared edit access
how_to_run: Create a PostgreSQL role, database, and schema for listaway with the grants shown in the README
Create a docker-compose.yml using image ghcr.io/jeffrpowell/listaway:v1.18.2 on port 8080 with an env_file
Create a .env file with LISTAWAY_AUTH_KEY, PORT, POSTGRES_USER, POSTGRES_PASSWORD, POSTGRES_HOST, and POSTGRES_DATABASE
For source builds: run yarn --cwd web run build, then go run cmd/listaway/main.go
notable: Shared lists use a random string in the URL, so they can be opened without logging in
Supports email/password plus OIDC/OAuth2 single sign-on with documented setup for Google, GitHub, Microsoft, Auth0, and generic OIDC providers
Optional SMTP for password reset emails; without it, reset emails are logged to the console
Password reset links expire after 1 hour and can only be used once
Includes a devcontainer for a quick development setup
caveats: Requires an existing PostgreSQL server; no embedded database is described
Building from source needs Go, Postgres, Node.js, and Yarn installed or a devcontainer
Without SMTP configured, password reset emails are only logged, not delivered
